correctness.rationale: With \(\operatorname{col}(X)=v^\perp\), the full-model residual is exactly \(Zv\), while the null observed coefficient is \(U=q^\top\varepsilon\); Gaussian orthogonality makes \(U,Z\) independent standard normals. For a uniform observation permutation, \(q^\top Pv\) has values \(-\sqrt{2/n},0,\sqrt{2/n}\) with the stated masses, so conditional rejection reduces exactly to binomial tail counts in four angular wedges. Including the observed statistic in the source empirical distribution gives the stated order index \(k\). The Gaussian wedge probabilities, law-of-large-numbers limit for fixed \(\alpha<1/4\), and final \(n\)-limit follow directly. An independent recomputation reproduced the reported \(n=20,m=1000,\alpha=0.05\) size to machine precision.
risks: The construction is rank-one residual and the exact formula is tied to the unstudentized one-sided statistic and the source empirical-quantile convention.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an explicit Gaussian boundary family where a widely motivated residual-permutation construction has severe size inflation despite ideal iid errors, with an exact finite-randomization formula and limiting size approaching one half. That sharply delineates the low-dimensional validity theory and is a substantive failure mechanism rather than a numerical anomaly.
risks: It is an explicit saturated family, not a worst-case theorem over all high-dimensional designs or other permutation procedures.

limitations: Even \(n\ge4\), saturated \(p=n-1\) design, iid Gaussian errors, full-model ordinary residuals, one-sided unstudentized coefficient statistic, and the source empirical-quantile rule only.
